newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine clergyman slams charter change moves.
newsitem.headline: Philippine clergyman slams charter change moves.

text.p: The Philippine's most influential prelate told Filipinos on Monday to be ready to revive "people power" protests to thwart moves to change the constitution, warning that "tyranny can come step by step."

"What we were were ready to die for in February 1986, we should be ready to fight for again... If need be, we will be there again," Cardinal Jaime Sin said, joining a clamour against revising the constitution to allow President Fidel Ramos to stay in power after his term ends in June next year.

Sin made his call in the prepared text of a speech he was to deliver at a mass on Monday evening commemorating the 1986 "people power" revolt that toppled then-president Ferdinand Marcos and restored democracy in the Philippines.
Sin played a major role in the 1986 uprising by calling out a million Filipinos onto a major highway to surround and protect army mutineers, who included Ramos, against advancing Marcos tanks.
"We gather here to say what we said in '86 - ' Never again! Never again!'" Sin said in the text of his speech.
"We are reminded that tyranny can come step by step, gradually, by infiltration, not in one powerful act. We are reminded...that freedom is not lightly won, but may be, oh, so quickly lost."
The current constitution, a reaction to Marcos's 20-year rule, limits a president to only one term of six years.

Ramos has said he will step down in June next year when his term expires, but many have questioned his sincerity after aides revealed that members of his Lakas (People Power) party wanted the constitution changed to permit a second term.
